text: Git branching is a core part of version control, helping teams work on the same project without conflict. One common practice is using *feature branches*. These are separate lines of development where you can add a new feature or fix a bug without affecting the main codebase. Once your work is ready, you *merge* it back into the main branch. In many workflows, this is done through a *pull request*, which allows teammates to review the changes before merging. This structured approach keeps the project stable and organized, making collaboration smoother and reducing the risk of errors.
